title: Comparing aggregated and nonlinear measures of coordinative behaviors in immediate responder first aid groups: a controlled experimental simulation study
abstract: BACKGROUND: When accidents and disasters happen, emergent ad-hoc groups of immediate responders form to provide aid before the arrival of professional medical responders. Little is known about how immediate responders coordinate with each other over time and how that coordination affects the quality of the first aid that is provided. Emergency response is described as complex and chaotic, but methods for analyzing complexity have rarely been applied in the emergency response context. This exploratory study aims to compare recurrence quantification analysis and aggregated data analysis of coordination behaviors by immediate responders to predict performance in groups providing first aid in a simulated context. METHODS: Sixteen groups of three participants (N = 48, 58% male, 40% female, and 2% preferred not to answer) were recruited from a large university and the surrounding city in southern Sweden using convenience sampling. They took part in a simulated traffic accident scenario. Of the participants, 56% had prior first aid training, including 6 emergency response professionals who were individually placed in different groups. The first aid performance of each group was rated by three subject matter experts. Only the first 10 min and 28s of each scenario was included in the analysis to allow for direct comparison of the recurrence quantification analysis results between groups. The Co-ACT framework was used to code participants' coordinative behaviors, and the dynamics of the behaviors' structure were calculated using a multidimensional recurrence quantification analysis. The aggregated and dynamical structures of the coordinative behaviors (i.e. behaviors of team members coordinating teamwork) were evaluated for their predictive power with regard to first aid performance ratings. RESULTS: Two groups were excluded due to incomplete data, and the analyses were conducted on the remaining 14 groups. Rate of recurrence of coordinative behaviors was found to significantly predict first aid performance (p = .02, β = -0.57) while aggregated post-experimental measures of coordinative behaviors did not (Action implicit p = .37, β = -0.31, Action explicit p = .97, β = <0.01, Information implicit p = .99, β = 0.01, Information explicit p = .68, β = -0.14). The negative effect of recurrence rate of coordinative behaviors on first aid performance suggests that other behaviors not measured in the Co-ACT analysis (e.g., task work such as chest compressions or bleeding control) had more effect on the quality of the first aid that was provided, at least in the current scenario. CONCLUSIONS: The study shows the usefulness of controlled scenarios for studying complexity in provision of first aid. Additionally, the results provide initial evidence for the predictive power of recurrence rate on first aid performance in ad-hoc first aid groups. This exploratory study thus shows initial evidence of the usefulness of complexity methods to understand the emergency response context. These contributions have potential significance for both emergency response researchers and practitioners.

title: Screening for discordant outcomes in cochlear implant users: Classification based on ECAP amplitudes
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cochlear implant (CI) recipients show considerable variability in postoperative speech recognition outcomes. While electrically evoked compound action potential (ECAP) recordings are routinely available in modern CI systems, their usefulness in routine clinical practice as a potential outcome measure has not been systematically established. OBJECTIVES: (CI) above and at or below a benchmark of 30%, respectively. METHODS: Data from two independent clinical datasets were analyzed. The screening procedure was developed using data from Clinic 1 (postoperative ECAP recordings at 200 cL) and validated using data from Clinic 2 (intraoperative recordings at 230 cL). A transformation procedure, based on the regression between ECAP threshold and amplitude empirically derived within each dataset, was applied to convert ECAP amplitudes obtained at 230 cL in Clinic 2 into equivalent values at 200 cL, thereby enabling cross-centre comparability. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to derive a critical A-ECAP cut-off value targeting a word recognition benchmark of 30%. RESULTS: High A-ECAP consistently associated with high word recognition across both datasets, whereas T-ECAP showed no comparable consistency. A critical ECAP amplitude of 121 µV (at a fixed stimulation level of 200 cL) yielded 100% specificity in the derivation dataset. In the validation dataset the positive predictive value was 94%, with five of 165 recipients showing a discordant outcome, defined as an amplitude above the criterion combined with poor word recognition CONCLUSIONS: Tools for recording ECAP are well established in clinical routine, but little attention is given to the information these responses carry regarding speech recognition. A large ECAP amplitude was consistently associated with good word recognition, whereas ECAP threshold was not. ECAP amplitude does not predict individual outcome. Its value lies in identifying discordant cases - a large amplitude combined with poor word recognition - in which the outcome cannot be attributed to the peripheral response and further evaluation, beginning with the fitting, is indicated. Whether these recipients benefit from re-intervention requires prospective evaluation.

title: Computational Models of the Foreign Body Response: A Focus on Biomaterial Properties
venue: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part A
abstract: The foreign body response (FBR) is the main biological process governing the long-term performance and safety of implantable biomaterials. As the FBR is complex, multifactorial, and unfolds over extended time scales, making in vitro replication challenging, standard biological evaluation frameworks continue to rely primarily on in vivo testing In this context, computational modeling offers a promising strategy to improve the fundamental understanding of FBR mechanisms, support biomaterial design, and reduce dependency on animal experimentation. Existing approaches, including ordinary differential equation (ODE), partial differential equation (PDE), and agent-based (AB) models, have provided important insights into inflammatory signaling, macrophage dynamics, fibrosis progression, and capsule formation. However, most computational models still treat the FBR in a simplified way and rarely integrate material-dependent effects in a quantitative manner, despite the well-established role of surface chemistry, topography, stiffness, and other properties in shaping host responses. This review summarizes the current state of the art in computational models of the FBR, including both mechanistic and data-driven methods, with a particular focus on how material properties are represented. We discuss the main limitations of current modeling approaches as well as the scarcity of standardized experimental data suitable for calibration and validation, and highlight the need for closer interplay between hybrid predictive models and experimental data, with a digital twin (DT) of the FBR representing the ultimate objective of these efforts.

title: “Absolutely Pure, Therefore Best”? Manufacturing “Purity” in the British Cocoa and Chocolate Industry, c.1850–1939
abstract: Beginning with the famous advertising slogan for Cadbury’s Cocoa, “Absolutely Pure, Therefore Best,” this article examines how British cocoa and chocolate manufacturers shaped evolving meanings of food purity to their advantage across legislative and commercial domains, from the 1850s until the eve of the Second World War. The article applies a cultural history lens to discourses of food adulteration produced by government-appointed select committees, contemporary publications in newspapers, journals and magazines, advertising materials, and extant corporate archives. Through close readings of these texts, the article argues that the purity of cocoa and chocolate became guaranteed less by unadulterated closeness to colonial-sourced cocoa beans and more by the complicated manufacturing processes, hygienic factories, and employment practices of the large confectionery manufacturing firms. These firms traded on their trusted reputations – linked implicitly in the case of Rowntree, Cadbury and Fry, to their Quaker family origins, and to paternalistic treatment of a white, female-dominated factory workforce – to influence contemporary legal, commercial and popular definitions of “pure” food. In the context of public anxiety over food safety in the period 1850-1939, manufacturers attached gendered, racialized and classed meanings of “purity” and “safety” to cocoa and chocolate as commodities, and to the processes of their production, which enhanced their status as nutritious yet always distinctly industrial foods.

title: Effects of A Speech-Clarity-Optimized TV Soundbar on Listening Experience in Older Adults with Age-Related Hearing Loss
abstract: Purpose: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) reduces high-frequency audibility and speech intelligibility during TV viewing, a major daily activity of older adults. This study compared a speech-clarityoptimized TV soundbar applying hearing-aid-based signal processing in three modes of increasing strength (M1-M3) with two commercial soundbars (A, B).Methods: Thirty-two older adults with ARHL (age, 74.8 ± 7.1 years; better-ear four-frequency pure-tone average [PTA], 46.9 ± 9.0 dB HL) participated in a participant-blind, within-subject study. Participants rated TV news presented through five conditions in randomized order at approximately 65 dB sound pressure level on a 10-item, 7-point questionnaire covering clarity, listening effort, sound quality, and satisfaction. All participants were tested unaided, and 25 hearing-aid users were also tested aided. Analyses used a linear mixed-effects model and Pearson correlation.Results: Listening scores differed significantly across conditions (χ² (4) = 171.91; p < 0.001), without a significant condition × session interaction. In the unaided session, M3 received the highest score (5.26 ± 2.05), exceeding A (3.00 ± 2.05) and B (2.89 ± 1.95), and scores increased with processing strength (M1 < M2 < M3) across sessions and domains. M3 was chosen as the clearest condition by 75.0% of participants. Poorer PTA was associated with lower absolute scores (M3: r = -0.73; p < 0.001), but not with the M3-A difference (r = -0.07; p = 0.696).Conclusion: The strongest mode of the speech-clarity-optimized soundbar received higher TV listening ratings than the commercial soundbars across the hearing-loss range examined. Objective speech-recognition testing should confirm these findings.

title: Technocentric Epistemic Injustice Beyond Identity-Based Prejudice
abstract: Abstract It has been argued that users of augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) are prone to a distinct kind of discrimination called speechism, due to their mode of communication being deemed inferior. This kind of discrimination originates from pervasive ableist oppression and thwarts users’ ability to have their experiences adequately heard in social settings, in which it is implicitly presumed that the only body capable of epistemic contribution is the able-bodied. This paper argues that speechism is akin to epistemic injustice, and more specifically to testimonial injustice. Speechism, however, highlights a gap in current epistemic injustice theory, as speakers suffering from testimonial injustice are usually thought to be the victims of some form of negative stereotyping and identity-based prejudice. In the case of AAC and speechism, I argue that the prejudice that results in epistemic injustice is not necessarily directed against the speaker but rather the medium that the speaker uses to communicate. As such, I defend the view that traditional epistemic injustice theory, as defended by Miranda Fricker, focuses too much on the speaker themselves and overlooks how modes of communication can also be vectors of testimonial injustice beyond being mere heuristics for negative stereotyping. I refer to this kind of epistemic injustice as technocentric epistemic injustice, where the technological means that allow for epistemic contribution and not the speaker themselves are prejudiced against.

title: Clinical outcomes and complications of Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA)-Based packing in otolaryngologic procedures: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background To manage bleeding and postoperative complications in endonasal surgeries such as septoplasty, turbinoplasty, and sinus procedures, nasal packing is commonly used. It achieves hemostasis, supports nasal tissues, reduces adhesions or stenosis, and promotes healing. This systematic review evaluates the clinical effectiveness and safety of PVA-based nasal packing compared to alternative materials in ENT procedures. Methods A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, ScienceDirect, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar covering 12 years and 2 months (1 January 2013 to 28 February 2025) to identify studies reporting the use of PVA in surgical procedures. Results A total of 31 studies met the inclusion criteria. The most commonly assessed outcomes included bleeding control, pain, patient comfort, recovery, and safety. Most studies compared PVA-based nasal packs with alternative haemostatic methods such as septal splints, Balloon Nasal Packs, bioresorbable nasal packs, silicone splints, and suturing techniques in septoplasty and endoscopic nasal surgery, focusing on hemostasis, healing, adhesion formation, and patient tolerance. Medicated Merocel was also reported to improve postoperative pain control, and its use in epistaxis management has been compared with devices such as Rapid Rhino, Posisep in terms of efficacy and complications. Conclusions Favourable hemostatic outcomes were reported with PVA based nasal packaging compared with alternative materials. PVA-based materials showed effective bleeding control and reliable postoperative haemostasis in ENT surgery, with the choice of agent tailored to surgical requirements and patient comfort.

title: Datacenter Metrics and Key Performance Indicators: Thematic taxonomy with verification status, formulas and proposed indicators
abstract: This document is a thematic taxonomy of the metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) used, or proposed, to describe datacenters from chip to site and beyond the site boundary. It lists 619 metrics and measurements and 266 candidate KPIs in 28 families, grouped into seven sections: energy and electrical systems; thermal management, water and environment; IT systems and workloads; sustainability, lifecycle and integrated performance; reliability, resilience and service; capacity, operations and economics; and safety, security and governance. Each entry has a stable identifier and a definition; metrics carry a unit, KPIs a formula written with metric identifiers and a direction. Every entry also records its origin, a verification status against primary or secondary sources, a maturity class (117 standardized, 647 in use, 121 proposed), its measurement level from chip to organisation, and dimension flags for sustainability, efficiency, security, health and safety, and economics. A listed KPI is a candidate: it becomes a KPI only with an objective, a target and an owner. Cooling is split into the facility plant, the air path and direct liquid cooling, with KPIs that compare the liquid path with the whole site. calculation pipelines and a gaming-risk checklist, and draws the catalogue as hypergraphs in which families, sections, dimension flags and measurement levels are hyperedges and identifier references are directed edges; hovering a node shows the definition of the entry. Abbreviations are defined under every table. The L A T E X source and the figures are generated by Python scripts distributed with the document.

title: Longitudinal Health Symptom, Treatment and Control Summary (2008–2026) A Longitudinal Synthesis of Symptom Burden, Autonomic Linkage, Intervention, Recovery and Present Level of Control
abstract: This document brings together 50 recorded health conditions or symptom complexes across the period 2008–2026. Its purpose is to show, in one longitudinal record, what occurred, how each problem may or may not relate physiologically to secondary autonomic dysfunction/MSAD, what treatment or management was used, what outcome followed, and the present level of control. The table is therefore both a chronology and a functional account of recovery, adaptation and continuing clinical burden. This is, fundamentally, a very personal medical log, arising from my own recordings, observations and continuing analysis of a complex health journey since 2008.

title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited. METHODS: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level). RESULTS: At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals. CONCLUSIONS: Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

title: Self-powered neural intervention via piezoelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are electromechanical energy-conversion devices constructed from piezoelectric materials. They convert physiological motion, local tissue deformation, or externally applied mechanical stimuli into localized electrical signals and have attracted considerable interest in self-powered neural interventions. Despite the rapid expansion of research in this field, the systematic understanding needed to guide translational optimization remains limited. This review delineates the current research landscape by organizing the discussion around mechanical inputs, piezoelectric transduction, neural responses, and functional restoration, thereby linking fundamental principles with representative application studies. This review discusses neural-interface-compatible materials, device architectures, and powering strategies for PENGs; the underlying neurobiological mechanisms; and recent advances in their applications across the peripheral, central, and autonomic nervous systems, neurodegenerative diseases, and neural interfaces. It further examines key barriers related to the precision of deep-tissue targeting, the long-term safety of implanted devices, and the lack of standardized frameworks for clinical translation. To this end, PENGs are systematically compared with other self-powered and wirelessly powered transduction technologies, and a standardized reporting framework linking device output to the biologically effective dose is proposed, while outlining future directions in multimodal energy coupling, closed-loop feedback, intelligent energy management, and the integration of piezoelectric stimulation with genetic, immune, and metabolic reprogramming. Collectively, this review aims to advance both fundamental research and clinical translation of PENGs in neural engineering.

title: Musical Sound Quality Perception of Low‐Frequency Degradation Across Hearing‐Assistive Devices
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare low-frequency-degraded musical sound quality perception between users of different hearing-assistive devices. METHODS: Fifty-two adults including 11 normal-hearing (NH) listeners, eight bilateral hearing aid users (HAHA), 17 bimodal users (CIHA), and 16 bilateral cochlear implant users (CICI) were recruited for a cross-sectional observational study. Participants assessed the sound quality of 3-s-long musical segments (15 sets) using the CI-Multiple Stimulus with Hidden Reference and Anchor test. Subjects rated and ranked a hidden Reference ("best"); three high-pass filtered (HPF) versions with low-frequency cutoffs at 200, 400, and 800 Hz; and an anchor (most degraded version). ART ANOVA with post hoc comparisons was conducted to identify between-group differences in average perceived sound quality ratings for each stimulus version. RESULTS: Both cohort and degree of low-frequency degradation had significant effects and interaction on sound quality perception (p < 0.001). HAHA users rated sound quality higher than both CIHA and CICI users for the 200 and 400 Hz HPF conditions (p < 0.001), while CIHA and CICI performed similarly. No difference was seen at 800 Hz HPF, suggesting all three hearing-impaired groups were similarly affected when low-frequency degradation was severe. Additionally, HAHA, CIHA, and CICI all had difficulty identifying the Reference and correctly ordering stimuli compared to NH. CONCLUSION: HAHA users exhibit superior sensitivity to low-frequency sound degradation (≤ 400 Hz) than CI users. These findings elucidate low-frequency perception limitations as a contributing factor to diminished CI-mediated musical sound quality and provide evidence for preoperative counseling of implant candidates regarding their postoperative music-listening experience.

title: What makes Chinese ancient-style pop songs appealing? The roles of song quality and emotional resonance
abstract: Chinese ancient-style pop songs integrate traditional cultural elements with contemporary popular music, and have developed a relatively stable audience base, but the mechanisms underlying listeners’ song preferences remain insufficiently understood from a systematic empirical perspective. Based on Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) theory, this study builds a research model with lyric quality, melody quality, arrangement quality, audio production quality and vocal performance quality serve as antecedents, emotional resonance acts as a mediator, and song liking is treated as the outcome variable. Through 924 valid questionnaires, this study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed hypotheses, and applies Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IMPA), Relative Importance Analysis (RIA), and a procedure for assessing out-of-sample predictive power (PLSpredict) to examine factor importance, ranking robustness, and predictive relevance. The results show that all five song components have a significant positive impact on emotional resonance and song liking. Emotional resonance also significantly improves song liking and plays a complementary partial mediating role. Further analysis shows that emotional resonance is the primary factor affecting song liking; among the components of songs that can be optimized, lyric quality is the most critical, followed by vocal performance quality. The PLSpredict results further demonstrate that the model has good out-of-sample predictive relevance. This study extends the application of SOR theory in the study of music acceptance, and provides an empirical basis for the creation and production optimization of Chinese ancient-style pop songs.

title: Approaching Modified Design and Operation of Fire Safe Facilities at Ahsanullah University of Science & Technology
abstract: In universities, fire accidents pose a severe threat to the lives and properties of teachers and students, because fire evacuation is difficult due to the dense population, numerous experimental instruments, and various flammables and explosives on campus. This paper explores deep into the fire safety of university buildings, and analyses the types and hazard sources of fire on campus. The objective of this research report is to discuss the primary issues concerning university buildings and to provide a modified layout for the fire safety design of university buildings that comprehensively integrates all aspects of fire safety. The paper classifies the factors that make university facilities a high-risk type of buildings to fire; reviews causes of fires in universities and identifies potential high-risk areas to fires in university facilities; provides modified layout and reviews design and operation factors controlling fire severity. Due to the absence of fire facilities in the present architecture, this article proposes a significantly improved fire plan that increases fire safety in all dimensions. Finally, the research is summarized, and the corresponding opinions and suggestions are given for the university fire safety management.

title: Realizing Low-Precision Storage and Sparse Execution in a Folded FPGA Speech Enhancer
abstract: Hardware-aware training often optimizes FPGA resources, latency, or bit operations, but folding changes what compression saves: shared arithmetic decouples precision, weight storage, and scheduled work. We derive training objectives from the measured costs of a folded streaming speech-enhancement accelerator. Mixed-precision weights reduce on-chip storage; structured channel sparsity removes entire operations from the engine schedule. We deploy a bit-exact implementation on the Kria KV260. The best sparse model eliminates 47.3% of convolution MACs, cutting frame time by 45% (1.86 to 1.03 ms) and dynamic energy by 60% (83 to 33 $μ$J/frame) against a storage-priced model measured in the same session, with higher speech quality. Relative to the most efficient dense build measured separately, frame time falls by 42% and energy by 48%. Reducing weight width from 8 to 6 bits lowers dynamic power by 27% but changes frame time by less than 5%. Plain channel group-lasso removes more work than cycle-cost-weighted lasso. Thus, folded-accelerator training should price storage and removable work separately, rather than rely on a single bit-operation metric.
